title: Directions and transportation: getting where you're going
title_target: ໄປແນວໃດ — Pai neeo-dai
goal: Ask for directions, understand the answer, bargain over a tuk-tuk fare, and tell the driver to stop in the right place — in sentences short enough to use while standing at the roadside.
bekal: ask for directions with ໄປແນວໃດ and ຢູ່ໃສ
bargain over the fare with ຄ່າລົດເທົ່າໃດ
tell the driver to stop with ຈອດ
ask about distance with ໄກບໍ່ and ຈັກກິໂລ

dialogs.title: ບົດສົນທະນາ — To Wat Sisaket by tuk-tuk
dialogs.intro: Budi is bargaining for a ride. Notice that the price is always agreed BEFORE getting in — there's no meter, and asking halfway there is too late.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ສະບາຍດີ|Sa-baai-dii] [ໄປ|Pai][ວັດ|wat][ສີສະເກດ|Sǐi-sa-kèet][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: Hello. Can you take me to Wat Sisaket?

lines.speaker: ຄົນຂັບ:
lines.text: [ໄປ|Pai] [ຄ່າ|Khàa][ລົດ|lot][ຫ້າ|hāa][ສິບ|síp][ພັນ|phán]
lines.id: Sure. The fare is fifty thousand.
lines.literal: go. cost — vehicle — five — ten — thousand.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ແພງ|Pheeng][ໄປ|pai] [ໄກ|Kai][ບໍ່|bàw] [ຈັກ|Ják][ກິໂລ|ki-lóo]
lines.id: Too expensive. Is it far? How many kilometers?

lines.speaker: ຄົນຂັບ:
lines.text: [ບໍ່|Bàw][ໄກ|kai] [ສາມ|Sǎam][ກິໂລ|ki-lóo][ເທົ່າ|thao][ນັ້ນ|nân]
lines.literal: not — far. three — kilo — only — that.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຄັນ|Khán][ຊັ້ນ|sân] [ສາມ|sǎam][ສິບ|síp][ພັນ|phán][ໄດ້|dâi][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.literal: if — so — three — ten — thousand — can — (question)?

lines.speaker: ຄົນຂັບ:
lines.text: [ສີ່|Sìi][ສິບ|síp][ພັນ|phán] [ຂຶ້ນ|Khʉ̂n][ມາ|maa][ເລີຍ|lóei]
lines.literal: four — ten — thousand. get-on — come — right-away.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ໄດ້|Dâi] [ໄປ|Pai][ແນວ|neeo][ໃດ|dai] [ຜ່ານ|Phàan][ຕະຫຼາດ|ta-làat][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: Okay. Which way do we go? Past the market?
lines.literal: can. go — way — which? pass — market — (question)?

lines.speaker: ຄົນຂັບ:
lines.text: [ຜ່ານ|Phàan] [ໄປ|Pai][ຊື່ໆ|sʉ̂ʉ-sʉ̂ʉ][ແລ້ວ|lèeo][ລ້ຽວ|lîao][ຂວາ|khwǎa][ຢູ່|yùu][ໄຟ|fái][ແດງ|deeng]
lines.id: Yes. Straight ahead, then right at the traffic light.
lines.literal: pass. go — straight-straight — then — turn — right — at — fire — red.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ວັດ|Wat][ຢູ່|yùu][ເບື້ອງ|bʉ̂ang][ໃດ|dai]
lines.id: Which side is the temple on?

lines.speaker: ຄົນຂັບ:
lines.text: [ເບື້ອງ|Bʉ̂ang][ຊ້າຍ|sâai] [ຢູ່|Yùu][ກົງ|kong][ຂ້າມ|khàam][ຫໍ|hǎw][ພະແກ້ວ|Pha-Kêeo]
lines.id: On the left, right across from Haw Phra Kaew.
lines.literal: side — left. be-at — straight — across — hall — Phra-Kaew.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຮອດ|Hâwt][ແລ້ວ|lèeo][ບອກ|bàwk][ແດ່|dèe][ເດີ້|dòe] [ຈອດ|Jàwt][ຢູ່|yùu][ນີ້|nîi][ໄດ້|dâi][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: Tell me when we get there. Can you stop here?
lines.literal: arrive — already — tell — a-bit — (friendly). stop — at — here — can — (question)?

lines.speaker: ຄົນຂັບ:
lines.text: [ໄດ້|Dâi] [ຮອດ|Hâwt][ແລ້ວ|lèeo] [ວັດ|Wat][ຢູ່|yùu][ພຸ້ນ|phûn]
lines.id: Sure. We're here. The temple is over there.
lines.literal: can. arrive — already. temple — be-at — over-there.

notes: **ໄປແນວໃດ pai neeo-dai = "how do I get there, which way."** The word *ແນວໃດ neeo-dai* means "how" and always goes at the end. To ask where something is, use *ຢູ່ໃສ yùu sǎi*: *ວັດຢູ່ໃສ* (where's the temple).

**ຄ່າ khàa means "cost, fee," and goes in front of the thing.** *ຄ່າລົດ* (fare), *ຄ່າຫ້ອງ* (room rate), *ຄ່າອາຫານ* (cost of food), *ຄ່າໄຟ* (electricity bill). ⚠️ Don't mix it up with *ຂ້າ khàa* (to kill), which has a low tone.
**ແພງໄປ pheeng pai = "too expensive."** *ໄປ pai* after an adjective means "too, overly": *ໄກໄປ* (too far), *ນ້ອຍໄປ* (too small), *ຊ້າໄປ* (too slow). A cheap and very useful add-on.

**Agree on the price BEFORE you get in.** Tuk-tuks and songthaews have no meters, and a price you didn't agree on will be agreed for you at the destination. Asking *ຄ່າລົດເທົ່າໃດ* before stepping in is a must-do habit, not a sign of distrust.

**ຂຶ້ນ khʉ̂n = get on, go up; ລົງ lóng = get off, go down.** Both work for vehicles and stairs: *ຂຶ້ນລົດ* (get in a vehicle), *ລົງລົດ* (get out of a vehicle), *ຂຶ້ນຂັ້ນໄດ* (go up the stairs). The same word appears in *ຂຶ້ນລາຄາ* (prices go up).
**ຈອດ jàwt = "stop and park."** To tell a driver to stop, say *ຈອດຢູ່ນີ້ jàwt yùu nîi* (stop here). *ຢຸດ yút* also means stop, but more in the sense of stopping movement — not pulling over.

**ຮອດ hâwt = "to arrive, to reach."** *ຮອດແລ້ວ* (we're here), *ຍັງບໍ່ທັນຮອດ* (not there yet). ⚠️ This word is typically Lao; the Thai equivalent is *ถึง thʉ̌ng*, which also exists in Lao (*ເຖິງ*) but is more formal.
**ເບື້ອງ bʉ̂ang = "side," used for left and right.** *ເບື້ອງຊ້າຍ* (on the left), *ເບື້ອງຂວາ* (on the right). For turning, the verb is *ລ້ຽວ lîao*: *ລ້ຽວຊ້າຍ* (turn left).
**ກົງຂ້າມ kong khàam = "directly across from," and ຂ້າງ khàang = "next to."** These two words cover almost every location people give when explaining the way.

after: To give directions, Lao people string steps together with *ແລ້ວ lèeo* (then): *ໄປຊື່ໆ ແລ້ວລ້ຽວຂວາ ແລ້ວກໍຮອດ* — "straight, then right, then you're there." Simple and enough.

after: Notice the prefix **ລົດ *lot***, meaning "vehicle," which attaches in front of the type: *ລົດຈັກ* (engine vehicle = motorbike), *ລົດຖີບ* (pedal vehicle = bicycle), *ລົດໄຟ* (fire vehicle = train). If you hear *lot-* at the start, it's something that moves.

blocks.text: The last two sentences are your safety net. Saying *ຂ້ອຍຫຼົງທາງ* while showing an address on your phone almost always ends with someone taking you there — in Laos, helping a lost person counts as building *ບຸນ* (merit), and people do it gladly.

blocks.text: **ໂພດ *phôot*** is the twin of *ໄປ pai* for "too," and a bit stronger: *ໄກໂພດ* (way too far), *ແພງໂພດ* (way too expensive). Both are correct; *ໂພດ* sounds more Lao, *ໄປ* more neutral.

A practical note about distances in Vientiane: the city is flat and small, and most sights are within three kilometers of the Mekong riverfront. Before bargaining with a tuk-tuk, first ask *ຍ່າງໄປໄດ້ບໍ່* — the answer is often "yes," and walking in the late afternoon is the best way to see the city.
